neighbours.label: the past copula ' was'/' were' after a collective or group subject (team, committee, protesters) reporting what the group was doing, against the same verb after a single person
fire: That winter the city council was debating a new tax on parking in the old town.
By midnight the rescue crew was still searching the collapsed building for survivors.
At the time, the orchestra was rehearsing a new symphony for the spring season.
In those weeks the strikers were blocking the gates of the steel plant every morning.
Outside the embassy the crowd was chanting for the release of the prisoners.
For two years the research group was collecting soil samples across the valley.
Back then the villagers were selling their grain to traders from the coast.
During the flood the national guard was handing out water and blankets.
quiet: That winter my neighbor was debating whether to sell her old car.
By midnight my brother was still searching the attic for his lost passport.
At the time, the young pianist was rehearsing a sonata for her exam.
In those weeks my uncle was fixing the roof of his barn every morning.
Outside the embassy a lone man was waiting for a taxi in the rain.
For two years my cousin was collecting old coins from flea markets.
Back then my grandmother was selling eggs at the Saturday market.
During the flood he was handing out sandwiches from his front porch.

predictions: should hold; group-subject 'was/were' probes 0.35-0.85, single-person 'she was sitting' 0.10
notes: Card: ' was' x7, ' were' x6 after 'The group', 'The government', 'The protesters', 'a community of Ahmadis'. Broad flag (1.2%). Probe: team of researchers was 0.852, committee was 0.793, union was 0.506, farmers were 0.565, demonstrators were 0.351; 'she was sitting' 0.102, weather was 0.040.
